recentItems.title: Sibiya applies for bail as State opposes release over witness interference and flight risk
recentItems.description:
Suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya is applying for bail in the Randburg Magistrate's Court, facing five serious charges including rape, trafficking in persons and the alleged sexual grooming of a 16 year old girl.

 The State is opposing bail, citing concerns over possible witness interference and the risk of escape.

recentItems.title: The Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, arriving at the GCIS media briefing  #sabcnews
recentItems.description:
The Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation, Prof. Blade Nzimande, arriving at the GCIS media briefing to release the highly anticipated Report of the Ministerial Working Group on Science, Technology and Innovation Funding.

The Working Group was established in May 2025 by Minister Nzimande to assess and make recommendations on the impact of the withdrawal of external research and development funding by the United States of America from major South African collaborative biomedical, health, and clinical trial programmes—particularly those focused on HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis…

Credits: Patricia Visagie

recentItems.title: The ACC has announced its party president, Masizole Mnqasela, as its mayoral candidate  #southafrica
recentItems.description:
The African Congress for Change(ACC)has announced its party president, Masizole Mnqasela, as its mayoral candidate ahead of the upcoming local government elections in Delft. The party has also announced Nandipha Bixa as its ward councillor candidate. The announcements were made in TRA 5 informal settlement, where the ACC outlined its plans for Delft and highlighted issues affecting residents, including housing, basic services and living conditions.

Credit: Yonda Magubudela

recentItems.title: Madlanga Commission | Sibanyoni advised to invoke right against self-incrimination in pending   case
recentItems.description:
The Madlanga Commission of Inquiry has advised Mpumalanga taxi boss Joe "Ferrari" Sibanyoni to invoke his right against self-incrimination where questions could prejudice him in a pending criminal case. 

The intervention follows another clash between Sibanyoni and Chief Evidence Leader Advocate Matthew Chaskalson, who has been pressing him on an alleged multimillion-rand extortion scheme. 

Sibanyoni and three co-accused are facing extortion and money-laundering charges linked to allegations that mining businessman Tengane Ntuli was forced to make protection payments. 
Sibanyoni has maintained that questioning him on matters before the criminal court could have legal consequences for him and his co-accused.
